summary: Colonizer: Life on Mars is an interactive educational game designed to introduce players to the challenges of sustaining a human crew on Mars. Players manage a team of five astronauts over a 30-sol mission while balancing essential resources such as power, food, water, oxygen, shielding and morale. They assign crew members to different tasks, respond to unexpected events, upgrade their base and make decisions that affect the survival and success of the mission. The project turns concepts related to Mars exploration and astronaut mission planning into an accessible, interactive learning experience for junior astronauts.
details:
Colonizer: Life on Mars

Project Overview

Colonizer: Life on Mars is an interactive educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge – Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The project places players in the role of a mission commander responsible for leading a crew of five astronauts through a simulated 30-sol mission on Mars. The objective is to establish and maintain a sustainable Martian settlement while managing limited resources, responding to unexpected challenges, and making decisions that affect the crew's survival.

How It Works

Players begin by selecting a Martian landing site: Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, or Meridiani Planum. Each location offers different starting advantages.

Throughout the mission, players assign astronauts to essential activities, including:

  • Maintaining solar panels and managing electrical power.
  • Growing food in a greenhouse.
  • Drilling for underground water ice.
  • Operating oxygen extraction systems.
  • Reinforcing habitats and improving protection.
  • Conducting scientific research and exploration.
  • Experimenting with terraforming concepts.

Players must carefully balance six essential survival resources: power, food, water, oxygen, shielding, and crew morale.

Challenges and Learning

The game introduces unexpected events such as dust storms, equipment failures, discoveries, and supply opportunities. Players must evaluate situations and make decisions while considering the consequences for the entire crew.

Three mission goals provide different approaches to success:

  • Scientist: Focus on exploration, discoveries, and scientific knowledge.
  • Terraformer: Develop progress through terraforming experiments.
  • Survivor: Complete the mission while maintaining the crew's essential resources.

An interactive Mars Codex also introduces players to real scientific information about Mars, including its atmosphere, gravity, dust storms, water history, and NASA's MOXIE oxygen experiment.

Technology Used

The project was developed as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It runs directly in a modern web browser without requiring additional software installation.

Educational Impact

Colonizer aims to make planetary exploration more accessible and engaging for younger learners. Instead of simply reading about space missions, players experience the responsibility of managing an astronaut crew and understand how interconnected decisions involving energy, food, water, oxygen, safety, and teamwork can be.

The game encourages critical thinking, resource management, scientific curiosity, and problem-solving.

Project Scope

Colonizer is an educational game and simplified mission-management simulation. Its resource values, events, and mission outcomes are designed for gameplay and learning; they are not predictions or validated engineering models of an actual NASA Mars mission.
